verified_signals.signal: Accessibility: voice-guided cash withdrawal was 'extended nationally' across ATMs and MFMs per the Q1-2026 release (04/05/2026); the bank's accessibility page describes assisted voice technology for the full cash-withdrawal process, personal headsets, relief symbols, Braille-marked cards issued since 15/05/2024, and cites Law 232/2022 (Romania's transposition of EU Directive 2019/882, the European Accessibility Act). The bank's public locator exposes a 'wheelchairAccessible' flag on all 263 branches (233 true / 30 false) but NO accessibility attribute whatsoever on any of the 1,806 self-service devices - so customers cannot tell which devices are voice-guided.
verified_signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Romania - Accesibilitate page and Q1-2026 BVB release; locator API; Directive (EU) 2019/882 Art. 32 for the deadlines
verified_signals.implies: Under Directive (EU) 2019/882 Art. 32, service providers may keep using products lawfully used before 28/06/2025 until 28/06/2030, and self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run until the end of their economically useful life but no more than 20 years after entry into use. That is a hard, dated replacement driver across the self-service estate, plus a lever for accessible self-service hardware and per-device compliance reporting - the missing per-device accessibility attribute is itself a concrete reporting gap to sell against.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - the 28/06/2030 transitional deadline is statutory, not discretionary
verified_signals.followup: Establish which units are already EAA-compliant and how many pre-28/06/2025 terminals fall inside the 20-year cap; check for ANPC enforcement action against banks
verified_signals.verifier_note: CORRECTED ON TWO POINTS. (1) SOURCING OF THE DEADLINES: I opened the bank's accessibility page directly. It confirms the voice-support technology, headsets, relief symbols, Braille cards from 15/05/2024, and it does cite Law 232/2022 transposing Directive 2019/882 - but it does NOT state 28/06/2025, 28/06/2030 or any 20-year rule. The researcher presented those as if sourced from the bank. I verified them independently against the Directive itself: Art. 32 gives the 28/06/2030 transitional end date for service providers and the 'end of economically useful life, but no longer than 20 years after their entry into use' cap for self-service terminals in use before 28/06/2025. Attribution corrected in the signal text so nobody re-checks the bank page and finds nothing. NOTE ON THE SOURCE ROUTE: eur-lex.europa.eu was unreachable - WebFetch returned an empty body and a desktop-UA curl returned HTTP 202 with 0 bytes - so the Article 32 text was verified via legislation.gov.uk's reproduction of the Directive. Logged in residual_gaps; an EUR-Lex citation should replace it when the site is reachable. (2) THE LOCATOR CLAIM WAS OVERSTATED: the researcher wrote the locator exposes NO per-device accessibility attribute. Enumerating every field name in the raw feed, a 'wheelchairAccessible' boolean DOES exist - but it is present on all 263 BRANCH records (233 true, 30 false) and on ZERO of the 1,806 ATM records, and no voice/audio/Braille attribute appears anywhere (string counts for vocal/audio/braille/nevaz/accesib across the feed: all zero). The corrected version is sharper than the original: the bank already ships an accessibility field for branches and simply has none for devices.

Raiffeisen publicly disputes the findings and has said it will litigate.

If provisioned it compresses 2026-2027 discretionary technology capex exactly while the Garanti integration is being funded - which argues for opex/managed-service and as-a-service commercial structures rather than capex hardware deals. Treat as a commercial-structure driver, not a sized opportunity.

verified_signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank S.A. - Raport anual 2025 (audited, PDF)
verified_signals.implies: Retail cash has been pushed overwhelmingly onto self-service, so device availability and cash-cycle efficiency are business-critical rather than convenience features. Strengthens the case for cash-forecasting/optimisation and availability-SLA managed services - and makes any Garanti branches inherited with staffed tellers an immediate conversion target at closing.
verified_signals.likelihood: Garanti branches are a plausible conversion target once the acquisition closes in Q4-2026
verified_signals.followup: Establish how many of Garanti's 71 agencies still run staffed cash desks
verified_signals.verifier_note: The passage is confirmed verbatim in the annual-report text I extracted: 'Pentru operatiunile cu numerar, clientii au la dispozitie in principal reteaua de bancomate si multifunctionale 24/7, precum si solutii alternative specifice persoanelor juridice pentru depunerea de sume mari de numerar (tip cash box). Pentru incasarea ratelor la credite in valuta (EUR/CHF/USD) de la persoane fizice a fost mentinut un numar limitat de casierii dedicate.' CORRECTED AN OVERSTATEMENT: the researcher's framing said '100% of retail cash has been pushed to self-service' and called the cashless model 'complete'. The source says 'in principal' (principally), explicitly retains dedicated cash desks for FX instalments, and elsewhere in the same report lists 'Depuneri de numerar la casieria Bancii pentru clientii non-retail' as a live fee-earning service - so counter cash has not gone to zero. Softened to 'near-cashless' and 'overwhelmingly'. RE-TAGGED [STANDING - dated 2025], is_new=false: this is a 7-month-old description of a settled operating model; the dated forward hook (Garanti closing Q4-2026) is carried by the Garanti signal. I also removed the researcher's unsourced 'H2-2027' integration timing here, consistent with the correction made to the Garanti signal.

verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - market reference, data as at 31/12/2025, published by BNR ~17/05/2026] BNR payment-instrument statistics: 11,136 ATMs provided by resident payment service providers (+1,108 vs June 2025), 729,408 POS terminals (+161,396), 685,731 EFTPOS acceptance points (+120,300), and 28.63m active cards (+10.07% vs June 2025) of which 24.68m carry a cash-withdrawal function (+5.06%).
verified_signals.source_name: Agerpres, Economedia, Bursa and Digi24 reporting of BNR payment statistics
verified_signals.implies: Romania's ATM base is growing again after years of decline and POS is expanding fast. Raiffeisen's ~1,211 own devices are ~11% of the national ATM base while its ~40,000 EPOS terminals are ~5.5% of national POS - i.e. it is under-indexed on acquiring relative to its balance-sheet share, which is consistent with acquiring being where it must chase share. Macro context that frames the RoPay and POS signals; not itself a sized opportunity.
verified_signals.followup: Pull the BNR interactive statistics database directly for the H1-2026 update rather than relying on press reporting
verified_signals.verifier_note: All five figures corroborated across four independent outlets including Agerpres, the national news agency (11,136 ATMs +1,108; 729,408 POS +161,396; 685,731 EFTPOS +120,300; 28.63m active cards +10.07%; 24.68m with cash-withdrawal function +5.06%; all deltas measured against June 2025). I re-derived the researcher's two ratios and both hold: 1,211/11,136 = 10.9% and 39,983/729,408 = 5.5%. THREE CORRECTIONS. (1) OPP_SIZE: the researcher set XL. This is a macro market statistic with no addressable Printec spend attached; per the sizing rule a macro driver is Unscoped, so XL was wrong and would have inflated the unit's apparent pipeline. Changed to Unscoped. (2) DATE: source_date was given as 31/12/2025, which is the data reference date, not the triggering event. BNR published these statistics around 17/05/2026 and the citation now points at Agerpres of that date; primary URL upgraded from Digi24 to the national news agency. (3) Tagged [STANDING - market reference] with is_new=false. NOT RESOLVED: I did not reach BNR's own interactive statistics database, so this remains press-tier and confidence stays Low per the primary-source rule - the basis of BNR's 'ATM' definition (machines vs sites, and whether kiosks are included) is therefore unverified and must not be compared naively with the locator device counts.

residual_gaps:
OEM STILL UNNAMED (the standing gap, unresolved): no public source names the hardware behind the 603 multifunctional units, the 60 Smart Cashbox units or the ~40,000 EPOS terminals. Euronet has run ATM+POS end-to-end for the bank since 2003 and no brand is disclosed in the annual report, the management report, the Q1-2026 filing or the locator feed. This remains the single highest-value open question for this unit and cannot be closed from public disclosure - it needs a field/partner channel.

GARANTI 2025 ACCOUNTS - PUBLISHED BUT UNREADABLE (partially closes an operator request): Garanti Bank S.A.'s 31/12/2025 individual IFRS statements are now live at https://www.garantibbva.ro/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Garanti_Bank_Situatii_financiare_individuale_IFRS_2025.pdf (HTTP 200, 9.6 MB, 162 pages), so the researcher's operator request for this document is satisfied. However the file is image-only with no text layer - pdfminer returned 25-40 characters across pages 1-100 - so Garanti's CURRENT branch, ATM and POS counts could not be extracted. It needs OCR. The only primary network figure that survives verification is 71 agencies at 31/12/2024. Garanti's 2025 Pillar III report was not located.

EUR-LEX BLOCKED: eur-lex.europa.eu would not serve Directive 2019/882 - WebFetch returned an empty body and a desktop-User-Agent curl returned HTTP 202 with 0 bytes. Article 32's 28/06/2030 transitional deadline and the 20-year self-service-terminal cap were therefore verified against legislation.gov.uk's reproduction of the Directive rather than the official EU text. The substance is verified; the citation should be upgraded to EUR-Lex when the site is reachable.

COMPETITION COUNCIL STILL JS-GATED: consiliulconcurentei.ro remains behind an anti-bot challenge, as the researcher logged. Both the ROBOR reasoned decision and the Garanti merger communique were therefore verified only via press (multi-outlet, including Agerpres and news.ro) and juridice.ro. The ROBOR fine consequently stays press-tier and Medium confidence; it should not be promoted until the reasoned decision or the bank's own H1-2026 provision disclosure is obtained. Needs a real browser session.

BNR PRIMARY NOT REACHED: the payment-instrument statistics were verified across four independent outlets but not against BNR's own interactive statistics database, so the definitional basis of its 'ATM' count (machines vs sites; kiosks in or out) is unverified and must not be compared naively with the bank's locator device counts. Confidence held at Low.

RBI GROUP H1-2026: still unpublished as of 31/07/2026, so no updated Romania-segment ATM/MFM/POS data. Re-check in August 2026.

UNSOURCED CLAIM REMOVED: the researcher's 'gradual integration to complete in H2-2027' for the Garanti deal appears in neither BBVA's release nor the Competition Council communique and I could find no primary statement of an integration end-date. It has been struck from two signals. The only sourced forward anchor for the deal is the Q4-2026 expected closing. Similarly, the '-12% y/y' attached to Q1-2026 net profit is absent from the release and was removed; RON 367m itself stands.

NO SIGNAL DROPPED: all 14 signals were retained. Nine are confirmed against primary sources, five are partially-confirmed with corrections applied in place (Q1-2026 profit basis and branch-trend anchor; accessibility deadline attribution and the locator's branch-only wheelchairAccessible field; Garanti integration timeline; the overstated '100% cashless' framing; and the BNR macro signal's opp_size and date). Nothing was contradicted-and-worthless. Confidence is capped at Medium throughout, with the BNR macro signal at Low.
